acip: GONG GI RTAGS GNYIS PA MA GRUB NA, RTAG PA CHOS CAN, BYE BRAG GI BYE BRAG YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD BYE BRAG YIN, KHYOD BYE BRAG DANG BDAG GCIG TU 'BREL, KHYOD MA YIN ZHING BYE BRAG YIN PA'I GZHI MTHUN PA DU MA GRUB PA'I PHYIR,
wylie: gong gi rtags gnyis pa ma grub na, rtag pa chos can, bye brag gi bye brag yin par thal, khyod bye brag yin, khyod bye brag dang bdag gcig tu 'brel, khyod ma yin zhing bye brag yin pa'i gzhi mthun pa du ma grub pa'i phyir
english: Then I disagree with the second part of your original statement: it is not the case that unchanging things are an example of something which is characteristic of what is characteristic of a quality. If you do disagree, then let's consider unchanging things. They are too an example of something which is characteristic of what is characteristic of a quality, Because (1) they are characteristic of a quality; (2) they are related to characteristics of qualities in such a way that to be an unchanging thing is to be characteristic of a quality; and (3) there are many examples of things which are not unchanging things, but which are still characteristic of a quality.
